title: Travel & Places
text:
Jerash, Jordan
Jerash is an ancient city in northern Jordan and one of the best-preserved Roman cities in the world. The area has been inhabited for thousands of years, but the ancient city developed during the Hellenistic period and later became known as Gerasa. In 63 BC, the region came under Roman control, and Jerash became one of the cities associated with the Decapolis.
Jerash reached an important period of growth under Roman rule. Many of the ruins that remain today were built during this period, especially during the first and second centuries AD. The city became an important center for trade and regional life.

title: Travel & Places
text:
What Is in Jerash?
The archaeological site contains many remains from the ancient city. Some of the most important are the Oval Plaza, the long Colonnaded Street, the Temple of Zeus, the Temple of Artemis, the South and North Theaters, ancient public baths, city gates, and Byzantine churches.
One of the most recognizable monuments is Hadrian’s Arch. It was built in AD 129–130 to honor the visit of the Roman Emperor Hadrian to Gerasa. The large arch stood near the southern entrance to the ancient city.
Walking through Jerash today makes it possible to see how a Roman city was organized. Its streets, temples, theaters, public spaces, and columns show the scale and importance the city once had.

title: Travel & Places
text:
My Experience
Visiting Jerash gave me the opportunity to experience the history of Jordan in person. Seeing the ruins was very different from simply reading about ancient civilizations. Walking between the columns and through the remains of the city made it easier to understand how large and developed Jerash once was.
As a student of International Relations, I also find places like Jerash interesting because they show how the Middle East has historically connected different civilizations, cultures, and political powers. The site reflects Greek, Roman, Byzantine, and later Islamic periods of the region’s history.

title: Travel & Places
text:
Travel & Perspective
For me, travel is not only about seeing new places. It is also an opportunity to understand different cultures, histories, and perspectives. Visiting historical places like Jerash helps connect what I study with the actual places and societies that shaped the region.

title: What a chart can tell me
text: A chart makes some patterns easier to see, but it also reflects a series of choices. Which observations belong in the plot? What belongs on each axis? Which differences deserve attention?

title: What a chart can tell me
text:
One choice that matters
In a comparison of income and life expectancy, a logarithmic income axis changes the spacing of the values. That can help reveal patterns that are difficult to see when a few large values stretch the scale.

title: What a chart can tell me
section: What I still need to ask
text:
What I still need to ask
A visible association does not explain why the pattern exists. Before moving from description to explanation, I need to think about the research question, the data, and possible alternative explanations.
My next step is to describe the plot in one careful sentence, then write down a question it cannot answer.

title: Notes & Reflections
text:
Not every interesting question becomes a research project. This page is where I keep shorter observations, ideas, and questions that develop through my coursework, reading, and interest in international affairs.
My academic work has made me increasingly interested in how large global changes are experienced at the level of individual states. Economic transitions, geopolitical competition, migration, changing patterns of trade, and new technologies may be global developments, but governments respond to them in very different ways.
For me, the Middle East and Gulf provide an especially interesting setting for thinking about these questions. States such as Kuwait are navigating economic diversification while also responding to changes in energy markets, regional politics, technology, and the wider global economy.

title: Notes & Reflections
text:
Research & Academic Projects

Can Rentier States Successfully Diversify?
One question I have explored is whether economies that depend heavily on natural resource revenues can successfully transition toward more diversified and productive economies. Through research on rentier states, I examined the challenges of institutional reform, economic diversification, human capital development, and reducing dependence on resource revenues.
This topic is particularly important to my broader interest in the economic transformation of Kuwait and other Gulf states.



Economic Recovery After Conflict: Turkey and Syria
In a research project on Turkey and Syria, I examined the role that stronger regional economies can play in supporting weaker or post-conflict states.
The project considered trade, investment, financial assistance, and the political interests that can influence economic cooperation. It also raised a broader question about whether economic assistance primarily supports recovery or also advances the strategic interests of the states providing it.



Political Economy of Legal Immigration in Greece
I examined the relationship between economic conditions and legal migration in Greece, focusing on factors such as employment opportunities, unemployment, economic growth, and labor shortages.
This project helped me think about migration not only as a political issue, but also as an economic response to changing labor-market conditions.



Structural Adjustment and Economic Reform in Zimbabwe
As part of a group project on the politics of the global economy, I studied Zimbabwe and the challenges associated with economic reform and development.
The project examined issues including economic instability, poverty, agriculture, inequality, governance, and the difficulties governments face when attempting major structural economic reforms.



Public Trust in the Media
In another research project, I examined declining public trust in the media and the political divisions surrounding perceptions of news organizations.
The project explored how changes in the media environment, partisan differences, and the growth of new forms of communication have influenced the relationship between citizens and the press.



Czech Parliamentary Election Analysis
I also prepared an election analysis brief on the Czech parliamentary election.
The project involved examining the political environment surrounding the election, major parties and political issues, and the broader significance of the election for Czech politics.

title: Notes & Reflections
text:
What Connects These Projects?
Although these projects examine different countries and political issues, they share a common theme: understanding how political institutions and economic conditions shape the decisions of states and societies.
Through these projects, I have become especially interested in international political economy, economic diversification, development, institutions, and the relationship between domestic politics and changes in the international system.

text:
My academic interests lie at the intersection of international relations, political science, political economy, and applied data analysis. I am particularly interested in how political institutions, economic conditions, and international relationships shape the development and decisions of states.

International political economy: How do international economic relationships, trade, investment, and political interests shape the development of states?
Governance and political institutions: How do institutions influence economic development, political reform, and the ability of governments to respond to domestic and international challenges?
Economic development and diversification: How do states respond to economic change, reduce dependence on traditional sources of revenue, and develop more diversified economies?
Geopolitics and international relations: How do regional competition, international cooperation, and relationships between states influence domestic political and economic outcomes?
Post-conflict development: How can trade, investment, foreign assistance, and regional cooperation contribute to the economic recovery of states affected by conflict?
Applied data analysis: How can quantitative methods, regression analysis, GIS, and computational approaches help us study political and economic questions across countries?

title: Academic Interests & Research
text:
Featured Research Project

Post-Conflict Economic Development: Turkey and Syria
One of my research projects examined how stronger and emerging economies can contribute to the economic development of weaker or post-conflict states, using the relationship between Turkey and Syria as a case study.
The project focused on a broader question: What role do developed and emerging economies play in supporting the economic development of less developed or post-conflict states?
I examined how economic support can take different forms, including trade, investment, financial assistance, and regional economic cooperation. The project also considered the political side of these relationships. Assistance between states may contribute to economic recovery while also reflecting the strategic, economic, and geopolitical interests of the countries providing that support.
The Turkey-Syria case provided a useful way to examine the relationship between economic development and international politics because the two countries are geographically connected and their relationship combines economic, humanitarian, political, and strategic considerations.
This project strengthened my interest in international political economy and in understanding how economic relationships between states can influence development and recovery after conflict.

Other Areas I’ve Explored

Economic Diversification and Rentier States
Through my coursework, I have explored the challenges resource-dependent states face when attempting to diversify their economies. I am particularly interested in the Gulf and in how institutional reform, human capital, economic policy, and geopolitical change influence diversification efforts.


Political Economy of Migration
I have examined the relationship between economic conditions and legal migration using Greece as a case study. This work considered how labor demand, unemployment, economic growth, and labor shortages can influence migration patterns and government policy.


Global Economic Reform
Through research on Zimbabwe, I explored structural adjustment, economic instability, development, inequality, governance, and the political challenges associated with major economic reforms.

Data & Methods
My Applied Data Analysis coursework complements my studies in International Relations and Political Science by allowing me to approach political and economic questions empirically.
I have worked with R and RStudio for data cleaning, visualization, correlation testing, and regression analysis. I have also gained experience with GIS and computational social science, which allow me to examine geographic and cross-national patterns in political and economic data.
I am interested in continuing to develop these methods and applying them to questions involving international political economy, economic development, geopolitics, and the Middle East and North Africa.

title: Notes & Reflections
text:
Questions I’m Thinking About
Some of the questions that currently interest me include:

What does successful economic diversification actually look like for Gulf states?
How much can governments reshape economies that have developed around natural-resource revenues?
How do geopolitical changes affect the economic choices available to smaller states?
What role will technology and data play in the future of government and political decision-making?
How can quantitative evidence improve the way we understand political questions without losing their historical and regional context?

These questions do not always have simple answers. They are areas I hope to continue exploring as my academic interests develop.

title: Notes & Reflections
text:
From Data to Politics
Studying data analysis alongside International Relations has also changed the way I approach political questions.
Political arguments often involve broad claims about countries, institutions, economies, and societies. Working with quantitative methods has encouraged me to ask what evidence supports those claims, how concepts can be measured, and what conclusions the available data actually allow us to make.
At the same time, numbers alone cannot explain every political outcome. Understanding history, institutions, geography, and political context remains essential. I am interested in the space between these approaches and in learning how they can complement one another.

title: Notes & Reflections
text:
Looking Ahead
As I continue my undergraduate studies, I want this page to develop alongside my interests. Some notes may begin with something discussed in class, others with a political or economic development that catches my attention, and others with a question raised while working with data.
The purpose is not to provide a finished answer every time. It is to document the questions worth thinking about and how my understanding of them changes over time.
